summary: Steel tower, 30 m, that Alberta's register dates to 2015; listed as active and reached by air. No other source found describes it.

access.note: Register lists the tower as active with fly access (reached by air). No source found says whether the public may visit the site.

events.note: Register gives 2015 as the year of construction for the tower.

evidence.supports: Chipewyan Lakes record: steel tower, built 2015, 30 m tall
Chipewyan Lakes record: active, access mode fly (reached by air)
Chipewyan Lakes record: no weather station
Alberta operates 127 fire lookouts from April to October
evidence.quote: The province operates 127 fire lookouts from April to October

evidence.supports: Lookout operators detect about 30% of wildfire starts each year
evidence.quote: lookout operators detecting approximately 30% of wildfire starts each year

evidence.supports: Each operator covers a 40 km radius for locating and reporting fires
evidence.quote: each lookout operator is responsible for locating and reporting wildfires within a 40-kilometre (25-mile) radius

evidence.supports: Each lookout site is staffed by an observer, generally from April to October
evidence.quote: Each site is staffed by a lookout observer whose job is to watch for wildfire all day, each day, generally from April to October.

corrections.why: The register lists the tower as active with fly access. It does not describe the site as closed.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. Only the Alberta register row and two general Alberta pages were found. Two searches turned up no Chipewyan Lakes-specific history, and the search results held no lookout-specific pages for this tower. Brief built 2015 matches the register. Brief access closed is corrected to restricted (active, fly access). The register query is the all-records query (where=1=1) because the name-filtered query returned a server error. The agency name follows the Alberta.ca bears page wording; the brief said Alberta Wildfire. The brief gave no local unit, so the story names only the province.
